prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single-character image-to-3D modeling input, STILETTO body revision 1.
Reference 1 and reference 2 are existing authoritative Loopforge STILETTO character sheets. Create ONE full-body front-view neutral A-pose of exactly this robot. Preserve her narrow segmented black-chrome mechanical body, long tapered limbs, fitted layered torso/pelvis, elongated slit-visored helmet, small crimson-orange visor, steel/chrome edge highlights, restrained brass joints, recessed hinges, and dense but coherent industrial mechanical construction. Her anatomy must feel like the same character, not a generic sexy android or cartoon.
IMPORTANT revised arm design: she has NO HANDS, NO FINGERS and NO PALMS. Both forearms end in compact cylindrical keyed mechanical coupling sockets at the wrist position, clearly designed for interchangeable blade or welding tool modules. Show the BODY ONLY, with both tools removed. Maintain full forearm length, visible elbow hinge, small tool-coupling ring; closed metal dust cap at each distal end, no exposed flesh. Do not put blades, light beams or any weapon/tool next to the character or on her body in this image.
Orthographic straight FRONT camera, no perspective, no three-quarter view. Bilaterally symmetric relaxed A-pose, arms about 40 degrees away from vertical, elbows almost straight, legs shoulder width, feet planted pointing forward, all parts separated with clear negative space. Helmet level looking ahead. Entire character fits with generous margin. Single figure fills most of a portrait 1024x1536 image. Neutral medium-grey background; soft even neutral studio light shows all plates with minimal shadows. Clean realistic game-art surface, fine edge wear, no scratches as noise, not toy proportions. No text, labels, floor grid, scenery, inset views, props, glow halo, sparks, dramatic shadows or limb overlap. This is a practical production reference, not a poster.

Use case: stylized-concept. Modeling reference, STILETTO body v1.
Image 1 is the authoritative FRONT view of the exact robot to rotate. Image 2 is her original character sheet for rear construction only. Produce ONE full-body strictly orthographic BACK view of exactly the robot in image 1, keeping identical height, thin long-limbed proportions, A-pose joint positions, panels/materials and feet. Show the rear of the helmet, back, arms and legs, not a new design. Black chrome fitted mechanical plates, recessed metal hinges, slim mechanical waist, restrained bronze connections. Both forearms terminate in small keyed tool coupling cylinders at wrist positions; NO HANDS, fingers, palms, blades or installed tools. No extra backpack, hair, wings, cloth or oversized hoses. Slim long silhouette. Portrait 1024x1536, full body centered same margin as reference front, feet shoulder width, arms approximately 30–40 degrees from vertical. Plain medium grey background, soft even neutral studio light, no labels, text, inset, floor grid, sparks or bloom. This is a rear reference to reconstruct the SAME 3D robot, not a concept variation.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single isolated image-to-3D prop input for Loopforge STILETTO modular forearm blade.
Input image 1: authoritative STILETTO original character and maintenance-tool material/style reference. Input image 2: matching new neutral body whose small wrist coupling receives this tool.
Produce ONE detached rigid blade module, not a character or full arm. Side-profile orthographic view, mount at LEFT, tip at RIGHT. A compact black-chrome keyed cylindrical coupling sleeve at left, a narrow mechanical root with recessed brass hinge detail, then one very long elegant tapered slightly swept steel blade forming a continuous extension of a forearm. Blade extension approximately three times the sleeve length, overall length approximately 55 cm at human scale, cylindrical mounting diameter about 7 cm. It is a forearm prosthetic, not a hand-held sword: no handle, no grip, no fingers, no hand, no trigger. Its silhouette is a slender razor spear, NOT a broad sword, axe, claw or chainsaw. Crisp beveled black-steel surfaces, restrained polished cutting edge, fine real industrial construction matching Stiletto's black chrome. Tiny recessed amber/red power channel along the blade root, no strong glow. Thin cutting blade and solid protective root, no fragile trailing strips. Back of socket needs plausible mechanical attachment. Neutral grey background, soft even studio lighting, full prop centered with margin in a landscape image. No text, labels, dimension lines, insets, duplicate views, sparks, smoke, motion blur, visible energy beams, shadows of other objects or dramatic lighting. All luminous runtime effects will be added separately. Practical modeling reference.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: isolated image-to-3D modeling reference for a proposed Loopforge STILETTO interchangeable forearm laser-welder tool.
Image 1 is the approved style of her blade module: match its proximal cylindrical mounting sleeve exactly, and keep its polished black-chrome/aged brass material family. Image 2 is original STILETTO art, with a maintenance tool inset for functional industrial construction.
Create ONE detached compact laser-welder module, in near orthographic side view, mounting coupling at LEFT, business end pointing RIGHT. NO character and NO hand. Reuse the keyed black cylindrical mounting ring of image 1. After the ring, a compact tapered protective black-chrome cowl encloses ribbed heat sinks, a small brass coolant manifold, one close-fitting loop of reinforced cable within the silhouette, and a slim recessed copper/ceramic focusing nozzle at the rightmost end. The nozzle has a dark optical aperture with an unlit glass lens; beam is OFF. Slight angular taper and layered plates convey a sharp precision tool, slim enough to replace the blade on this thin robot. This must feel like a forearm prosthetic, not a pistol/rifle or hand-held welding gun. No handle, trigger, stock, grip, fingers, bulbous forms, giant hoses or sprawling attachments. Overall module length about 25cm and coupling diameter about 7cm. Entire object with generous margin on plain neutral-grey background and soft studio light. High-quality practical game concept art, believable mechanically coherent material construction, no labels, multiple views, text, dimensions, sparks, smoke, glowing beam or dramatic shadows.
